title: Zero-bubble load-use forwarding
motivation:
The current five-stage pipeline unconditionally stalls one cycle for every
load-use dependency, even though the Tang Nano bench presents combinational
zero-wait read data. CoreMark has frequent load-dependent address, compare,
and arithmetic instructions, so this bubble directly reduces iterations per
cycle. The existing P&R report also shows the EX/MEM-to-EX forwarding path as
the dominant timing path, making a dedicated load-data bypass a focused
high-value datapath optimization.

byte/half/word value into the EX operand mux, and remove the unconditional
load-use bubble. When dmemReady is low, hold the dependent instruction and

a bubble. This should preserve arbitrary bus-stall correctness while
improving CoreMark IPC on the zero-wait FPGA path.

# Implementation notes

## Changes

- Removed `is_lui` from the internal `ctrl_t` pipeline bundle.
- Kept the decoder's standalone `is_lui` output and decoder unit-test interface;
  `id_stage` still connects that output but no longer copies it into `ctrl_t`.
- Removed `branch_taken` and `branch_target` from `ex_mem_t`.
- Kept branch comparison, target generation, misalignment trapping, redirect
  generation, and `pc_next` resolution local to EX2.
- Removed only the EX/MEM payload assignments for those dead branch fields.

## Deviations and concerns

No architectural or valid/hold behavior changes were made. The local
`branch_taken` and `branch_target` signals remain in `ex_stage.sv` because
they are required by EX2 redirect and misalignment logic.

## Verification

- Verilator lint: pass.
- Formal: not executable in this environment. The repository harness points
  at a read-only shared `riscv-formal` tree, so its generated work directory
  could not be cleaned/created. A temporary writable copy generated the
  checks, but every SBY task failed before execution because the installed
  `sby` could not import Python module `click` (`ModuleNotFoundError`). No
  RTL counterexample was produced.

title: Isolate the RV32M multiply pipeline
motivation:
The current EX2 ALU structurally contains a full-width multiply alongside
the ordinary integer datapath.  The successful EX1/EX2 retiming shortened
the forwarding-to-ALU path, but ordinary CoreMark instructions still pay
the shared M-operation mux and routing footprint.  A dedicated, narrow
multiply lane is a more targeted structural change than another global
queue or front-end buffer.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Split RV32M multiplication from the base ALU into a small registered

buses and RVFI ports.  The isolated lane should reduce the normal EX2
cone and routing pressure while imposing latency only on the relatively
infrequent multiply dependency chains.

title: Single-entry JALR target cache
motivation:
The proven static predictor removes most direct-JAL and backward-loop
redirects, but JALR returns still resolve in EX and pay a redirect bubble.
Larger dynamic predictors and RAS variants regressed this fixture because
IF-stage decode, table lookup, or target selection extended the fetch
critical path. Repeated hot return sites are a narrower opportunity.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a one-entry EX-trained indirect-target cache for JALR control transfers.

title: Short-loop filtered backward prediction
motivation:
The existing backward-taken/direct-JAL predictor is the only predictor
family that improved this fixture, but it predicts every backward
conditional branch as taken.  That policy pays a full recovery flush for
backward control transfers that are not tight loops, especially uncommon
error or exit paths.  Dynamic tables, return predictors, and extra IF
lookups have already shown that their timing cost is too high for this
core, so the useful remaining opportunity is a stateless refinement of the
proven predictor.

title: Global forward-branch bias predictor
motivation:
The proven predictor already removes most backward-loop and direct-JAL
redirects, while indexed BHTs, RAS structures, and target caches have
repeatedly lost Fmax on this small FPGA.  Forward conditional branches
remain the main unpredicted control-flow class, but they need a predictor
with materially less lookup and routing overhead than a PC-indexed table.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one 2-bit saturating global direction counter used only for forward
conditional branches.  Initialize it weakly not-taken so reset behavior
preserves the current policy, let its MSB override the default only when
the fetched branch displacement is forward, and update it from each
resolved forward branch in EX.  Backward conditional branches and direct
JALs retain the existing static predictions, and EX remains authoritative
for mismatch recovery and RVFI pc_next.  A single counter avoids the
aliasing, tag compares, and multi-entry muxes that made prior dynamic
predictors expensive, while still adapting to CoreMark's phase-level
forward-branch bias.
